anomalies.observed: The two alternative MCU footprints for the same ATtiny45 disagree on the pin-to-net mapping of the POT and TACH signals. On the THT footprint U2, pin 2 (PB3/XTAL1) carries POT and pin 3 (PB4/XTAL2) carries TACH; on the SMD footprint U3 the assignment is reversed, with pin 3 carrying POT and pin 2 carrying TACH. All other pins (5=SDA, 6=PWM, 7=SCK, 1=RST) match.
anomalies.expected: U2 (ATtiny45-20P, marked THT) and U3 (ATtiny45-10S, marked SMD) are interchangeable packages of the same chip, so each physical pin must carry the same net on both symbols. The POT and TACH nets must be assigned to the same pin numbers on both footprints.

anomalies.impact: Populating the SMD footprint U3 instead of the THT U2 (or vice-versa) cross-connects the fan tachometer input and the analog potentiometer input: the R6 pull-up / R4-D1 clamp network intended for TACH ends up on the POT (ADC) pin, and the potentiometer wiper ends up on the TACH pin, breaking speed feedback and the set-point reading.

parsed.summary: The schematic is largely consistent (regulator, fan MOSFET/BJT driver, TACH clamp, POT divider all plausible), but the two interchangeable ATtiny45 footprints U2 (THT) and U3 (SMD) assign the POT and TACH nets to swapped physical pins (2/3), which is impossible for identical-chip alternative footprints and would mis-wire the fan feedback and set-point inputs on one of the two builds.
